title: Inter-Dominion Agreement on the Recovery of Abducted Women
note: In December 1947, India and Pakistan signed an inter-dominion agreement instituting a state-led recovery operation that searched for and repatriated an estimated 75,000 to 100,000 abducted and forcibly converted women across both borders, often against the women's own expressed wishes. Documented by feminist historians Urvashi Butalia, Ritu Menon, and Kamla Bhasin.

title: Rajkumari Amrit Kaur
note: Prominent Christian Indian freedom fighter, close associate of Mahatma Gandhi, and independent India's first Minister of Health (1947–1957). Played a leading role in managing massive Partition refugee transit camps in Delhi, establishing the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), and advocating for women's franchise.

title: Operation Polo and the Annexation of Hyderabad
note: Military action by the Indian Armed Forces against the princely state of Hyderabad in September 1948 following the Nizam's refusal to accede to India after the lapse of British paramountcy. The Sundarlal Committee report documented widespread communal violence during and after the police action.

title: Proclamation of Indonesian Independence
note: Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta read the Proclamation of Indonesian Independence in Jakarta on 17 August 1945, triggering the Indonesian National Revolution against returning Dutch colonial forces. Critical contemporary milestone in Asian decolonization alongside Indian independence.

title: Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) for the Partition of India
note: Radio broadcast and official announcement on 3 June 1947 by Viceroy Louis Mountbatten, Jawaharlal Nehru, Muhammad Ali Jinnah, and Baldev Singh announcing the principle of partition and accelerating British departure to August 1947.
